clue.text: Power at mains switch

indicators.note: to switch things round is to rearrange them, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Electricity flows when someone flips the switch at the mains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like the light switch of the surface, but it is the anagram signal working on AT MAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the endurance to keep going.

clue.text: Lead swinger in final of Olympics throwing event

indicators.note: the final of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the hammer is a track and field throwing event

explanation.surface: A competitor swings a lead ball in the Olympic hammer final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To swing the lead' is British for to malinger, so a lead swinger fakes illness; the hammer ball is the surface's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: One who swings the lead dodges work by pretending, a feigner.

clue.text: Sauna made exotic to a sickening degree

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, signalling the letters are made unusual

explanation.surface: A sauna is turned into something exotic until it is nauseating.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means repeated until disgusting or tedious.

clue.text: Magazine for kids

explanation.surface: A periodical for children.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one edition of a periodical, and issue means offspring in legal language.

clue.text: It has succulent shoots containing a well-inverted sugar

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, which reads the down word upwards

explanation.surface: A plant with juicy stems holds a well and some upturned sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' turns SUGAR into RAGUS; 'containing' joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is the vegetable whose edible young spears are tender stems.

clue.text: Consider fancy and speculate

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a whim and takes a guess.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: to suspect something is to consider it likely, to fancy it is so, and to speculate that it might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Each verb is a way of believing something likely without proof: 'I suspect', 'I fancy', 'I speculate'.

clue.text: Sailing-boat bought when football gamble comes up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: the pools are the football pools, betting on match results

explanation.surface: Someone buys a yacht after a big win on the football pools.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British weekly bet on match results.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Dundee petticoat tails?

parts.note: petticoat tails are a Scottish shortbread biscuit, and a petticoat's tails cut short suggest the word

explanation.surface: The hems of underskirts in a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a Scottish city known for its cake; petticoat tails are wedges of shortbread, and a short petticoat suggests cake that is short.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortbread is a crumbly Scottish biscuit-cake, like the petticoat tails served in Dundee.

clue.text: Boredom is a bit of a rotten nuisance

indicators.note: only a bit of the words is used, so the answer is found within them

explanation.surface: Tedium is partly a terrible pest.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'rottEN NUIsance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness from lack of interest.

clue.text: Tear in fashion as a part of new jersey, we hear

indicators.note: the word for tear goes in the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is fashion or style
a rent is a tear in cloth

explanation.surface: A fashionable new sweater gets a rip in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' tells the solver to say 'tear' to rhyme with 'bear', a rip, not a drop from the eye. 'New jersey' looks like a sweater; it is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenton is the state capital of New Jersey.

clue.text: Saint taking a long time to I accept opening of nunnery

indicators.note: a long time is made to accept, that is take in, the next letter
a long time is made to accept, that is take in, the next letter

parts.note: ages means a long time

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A nun-to-be waits ages before the convent finally lets her in.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the first letter of 'nunnery', goes inside AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: St Agnes is a Roman virgin martyr, patron saint of girls.

clue.text: They, for example, going to church with stress

parts.note: 'they' is an example of a pronoun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone goes to church to complain about the strain of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' looks like a group of people, but it is the word itself, a part of speech; 'going to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce a syllable is to sound it, as when giving it stress in speech.

clue.text: Leicester, say, poor in Len don marathon runner

explanation.surface: A poorly performing athlete from Leicester runs the London Marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Leicester is a cheese, and 'mousetrap' is slang for cheap, inferior cheese; Agatha Christie's play The Mousetrap has run in London's West End since 1952, the longest run of any play.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor cheese fit only for baiting traps gets the trap's name, and a show running for decades is a theatrical marathon.

clue.text: Stain article in hair-dye

indicators.note: the article goes in the hair-dye word

parts.note: a tint is a colour put on hair
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A hairdresser finds a mark left by the dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a mark of contamination or discolouration.

clue.text: Old cold rhubarb

explanation.surface: An elderly person with a chill is talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Rheum is a dated word for the watery discharge of a cold, and Rheum is the botanical genus of rhubarb.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is archaic catarrh, a running nose; the second is the plant's Latin genus name.

clue.text: Light outfit for clubs, say?

parts.note: minor means light or slight
a suit is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: Casual clothes for nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, clubs and diamonds are the minor suits, scoring less than hearts and spades.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, clubs are one of the two lower-ranking card suits.

clue.text: Carrying young, for example, going back to Paddington?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'for example' is read backwards

parts.note: Paddington is a London railway terminus, an example of a station

explanation.surface: A young bear is carried back to Paddington station where he was found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns EG into GE. Paddington is a London railway station (and the bear named after it); the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is pregnancy, the time a mother carries her unborn offspring.

clue.text: Greatness of a kind in some police officers

indicators.note: greatness of a kind is greatness in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some police officers have a certain kind of greatness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeants rank above constables in the police.

clue.text: Decimally, I have concentrated

parts.note: counting decimally is counting in tens
I've is short for I have

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of focusing on the decimal system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decimally' gives the phrase IN TENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive means focused and thorough, done in a concentrated way.

clue.text: Wolf more prudent to stay outside sultanate

indicators.note: the word for more prudent stays outside, wrapping the sultanate

parts.note: wiser means more prudent
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A wolf thinks it wiser to keep clear of a sultan's land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolf' is the slang for a man who chases women, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf, in slang, is a predatory seducer of women.

clue.text: Jacket in which women run paper-round

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: round signals the letters going round into a new order

explanation.surface: Women do a newspaper round wearing jackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the paper round of the surface but turns PAPER into APPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapper is a book's dust jacket, its outer cover.

clue.text: Crack up in Middlesex tol erated

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Collapsing with laughter is put up with in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'middlesEX TOLerated'. 'Crack up' looks like breaking down, but here means to praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack something up is to praise it highly, as in 'not all it's cracked up to be'.

clue.text: Lured, sailors say, in direction of shelter

indicators.note: this is how seafarers pronounce the word, as 'loo-ard'

parts.note: lured means enticed

explanation.surface: Sailors are enticed to seek shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors pronounce the answer 'loo-erd', the sound of 'lured'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side sheltered from the wind.

clue.text: Bill Hill has hard lines sometimes

parts.note: AC (account) is a bill
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A man named Bill Hill has a run of bad luck now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Hill' reads as a person's name, and 'hard lines' as British for bad luck; the lines are a performer's script.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer must learn lines, and some scripts are difficult.

clue.text: Leather strip, though no good when shrunk

indicators.note: shrinking the word cuts it to its short informal form

explanation.surface: Leather contracts badly when shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when shrunk' cuts THOUGH to its informal short spelling THO.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather used as a lace or whip.

clue.text: Green light given for depopulation

explanation.surface: Permission is granted for emptying an area of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland Clearances were the forced eviction of tenants from the Scottish Highlands in the 18th and 19th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is official permission to proceed, and also the emptying of a region's population.

clue.text: Friend in the country?

explanation.surface: A pal in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate'; British slang uses china for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: China is slang for a mate, and the name of the large Asian nation.

clue.text: Highly respected, say, his religion?

parts.note: a man whose faith treats the Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie as divine, the emperor's princely title before coronation giving the faith its name

explanation.surface: A respected man asks what religion he follows.
explanation.walkthrough: Haile Selassie's title before his coronation, meaning prince or head, began his name; the Jamaican faith that venerates him takes its name from it, and its follower is called by the short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Jamaican faith that reveres the Ethiopian emperor is known by the shortened name.

clue.text: Proof in Us perhaps of extravagance

indicators.note: perhaps signals that these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Evidence found in America suggests wasteful spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Profusion is lavish abundance, a great excess or prodigality.

clue.text: Small type of star, but a bright one

parts.note: pica is a size of printing type

explanation.surface: A minor sort of star is still a shining one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small type' looks like tiny print, but it is S plus PICA, a type size.
explanation.definitionFit: Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo.

clue.text: Meeting a target, perhaps, in Henley

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: An archer at Henley hits a target.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley Royal Regatta is a famous rowing event on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of boat races.

clue.text: The main pot for algae?

parts.note: the main is an old word for the sea
pot is slang for cannabis, weed

explanation.surface: Cannabis is being smoked to cure algae.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic phrase for the open sea; 'pot' is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp and wrack are marine algae, the plants of the shore.
